title: Promises and async / await
summary: How JavaScript handles things that take time, like loading data.
heading: Promises and async / await

blocks.text: Some things take time — loading data, a timer, an image. JavaScript doesn't wait around for them; it keeps going and deals with the result later. A Promise is a placeholder for a value that isn't ready yet. It promises to give you the result once it's done — whether it worked or failed.

blocks.caption: A Promise starts pending, then settles as fulfilled or rejected.

blocks.text: You can't use the value right away, so you hand the Promise a function to run once it's ready. .then(...) handles success, and .catch(...) handles errors. Press Run and wait one second.

blocks.code: Waiting...

blocks.text: Chaining lots of .then(...) calls gets hard to read. async / await lets you write code that waits, but still reads top to bottom like normal steps. await pauses until the Promise is ready.

blocks.code: Waiting...

items: A Promise stands for a value that will arrive later.
async / await is a cleaner way to write the same thing.
